scope: D6 and D7 conditional investigations; no capability implementation is claimed

d6.trigger: D0/D2 show large-environment import, extraction or local storage dominating the target workload; remote loading additionally needs a distribution bottleneck
d6.observed: The matched dependency fixture is 4 MiB. Composing it across 50 distinct workspaces reduces imported bytes from 211968000 to 4741120 and preparation from 7.644/7.228 to 3.215/3.027 seconds. Existing target measurements establish repeated setup and writable copy-up costs, but do not establish large-environment storage or remote distribution as the dominant cost.
d6.followup: Reconsider local EROFS with an actual large environment when its import/extraction/storage dominates. Measure CPU, I/O, cache reuse, startup tails and readiness before remote loading.

d7.measurementScope: Historical last canonical W0-protocol L9 checkpoint. D3 burst readers are not a new think-time capacity measurement.
d7.method: Extrapolate the maximum observed per-item idle cost among cohorts 1/10/50 to the passing population, divided by the minimum passing-trial median pool memory minus the full 512 MiB daemon ceiling. This conservative fixed-cost estimate is not a direct attribution of each loaded process.
d7.followup: Reconsider when a canonical passing capacity stage reaches the 40% idle-memory trigger. Require disk workspace, background-process protection, cwd/export and state-loss rules, measured released memory and resume cost. Keep the zero-swap reference; freezing alone has no established memory saving.

measurementPolicy: Checkpoint-only full density measurements remain L2/L7/L9. Keep raw attempts in CI artifacts or operator storage; retain performance misses as issues without repeated tuning in the same change.
